mentl/5aaccfe:
wasi_filesystem's own comment promises that "a function that doesn't reach
fs_* ops proves `with !Filesystem`", and that audit-driven severance then
drops path_open / fd_close from that binary. march_run, main's emit route
and mcp's gate created, wrote, renamed, closed and unlinked files through
the _impl fns instead. All three sit inside a ~> wasi_filesystem install —
march_run's entire body has the chain at its foot — so the ops were
reachable the whole time.

The bypass was invisible because the impls charge WASI, not Filesystem.
The row stayed truthful about the substrate and silent about the
capability, so !Filesystem kept holding over routes that write files. One
line of main.mn had both spellings in one expression:
fs_exists_impl(gen_path) beside fs_read_file(gen_path).

The effect had no op for what two of those routes do most. fs_create_impl
is genuinely distinct from fs_open_impl (WASI oflags CREAT|TRUNC and
write-only rights against CREAT and read/write), so writing a file had no
op to perform. fs_create(String) -> Int is declared and armed.

The gate is a verify tier asking the medium `refs of <impl>` for each of
the nine and counting sites outside the handler that owns them — the verb's
answer, not a grep, because a grep cannot tell a call from a name in a
comment. It corrected me immediately: my hand census found three bypasses;
the tier found thirteen more. The pre-fix number was then measured rather
than derived (stash the fix, re-run the tier) and read 24. Eleven
conversions, 24 -> 13, ratcheted monotone down.

The 13 are named, not accepted: space's file server, battery_libs (which
declares `with WASI`, so its row is honest about the substrate), persist,
dsp/cfc. Each wants its own install-coverage reading.

Recorded because it cost a probe: the natural gate would be a frontier
fixture declaring `with !Filesystem` and calling the ops. It cannot exist.
Filesystem is the compiler's own effect, so a checked user program has no
access to the vocabulary
